title: One-year-old AI startup with six employees acquired for estimated $100M
content:
One-year-old Israeli AI startup with six employees acquired for estimated $100 million
Rocket Software has acquired Geniez AI, whose technology uses AI agents to help enterprises manage and modernize mainframe systems.
U.S. software company Rocket Software has acquired Israeli startup Geniez AI in a deal valued at up to $100 million, according to estimates. The two founders, both graduates of Mamram, the Israel Defense Forces’ computing unit, received the acquisition offer one year after announcing their Seed round, with the company having a team of only six employees.
In September 2025, Geniez AI raised $6 million in a Seed funding round co-led by StageOne Ventures and Canapi Ventures. CEO Gil Peleg and co-founder Dan Shprung previously founded Model9, a mainframe data management startup acquired by BMC Software in 2023.
Geniez AI develops generative AI technology designed to help enterprises manage and modernize mainframe systems, the large-scale computers that underpin critical business operations across industries, including financial services. Its AI agents operate directly on mainframes, monitoring live systems, diagnosing incidents and executing workflows using natural language.
As part of the acquisition, Geniez AI’s technical leadership and engineering team will join Rocket Software to help accelerate its AI initiatives, including new capabilities for Rocket EVA, the company’s agentic AI platform for core systems. The companies aim to move mainframe management away from processes that depend heavily on specialized expertise toward AI-assisted operations that make complex systems easier to understand, manage and modernize.
Rocket Software said the acquisition would help enterprises address the shortage of skilled mainframe professionals, reduce operational complexity and automate mission-critical workflows. The combined technology is intended to help teams turn institutional knowledge into actionable intelligence, surface insights and take action across core systems while maintaining appropriate security, governance and control.
“Geniez AI was founded on the belief that GenAI-based business applications can fundamentally change how enterprises understand and operate their mainframe environments,” Peleg said. Joining Rocket, he added, would give the company the scale, customer reach and mainframe expertise needed to bring its technology to more organizations and help shape the next era of intelligent, mission-critical operations.
Milan Shetti, president and CEO of Rocket Software, said the acquisition would accelerate the company’s efforts to help enterprises securely apply agentic AI to their systems. He described the deal as part of Rocket’s broader strategy to modernize core systems while extending AI capabilities to the critical workloads that run on them.
Rocket Software is a privately held U.S. company headquartered in the Boston area that specializes in enterprise software modernization, including mainframe systems. The company says it serves more than 13,500 customers, works with 850 partners and employs over 3,000 people worldwide. It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Private Equity.

report.summary: Rocket Software acquires Israeli AI startup Geniez AI, a six-employee, one-year-old company, for up to $100M to bring agentic AI to mainframe modernization.
report.background: Mainframes still run the bulk of critical transactions in banking, insurance, airlines and government, but the workforce that understands them is retiring fast. Enterprises face a well-documented shortage of COBOL and z/OS specialists, rising operational costs, and mounting pressure to modernize without breaking mission-critical systems. Geniez AI entered this gap in 2024, building generative AI agents that monitor live mainframes, diagnose incidents and execute workflows via natural language. The founders, Gil Peleg and Dan Shprung, both Mamram IDF computing unit graduates, previously built Model9, a mainframe data management startup acquired by BMC Software in 2023. Geniez raised a $6M seed in September 2025 led by StageOne Ventures and Canapi Ventures, and was acquired roughly a year later. Rocket Software, a Bain Capital portfolio company serving over 13,500 customers, is betting that agentic AI can convert scarce institutional knowledge into automated operations.
key_points: Tiny team, huge exit: Geniez AI had only six employees and launched its seed round about a year before the acquisition. The estimated $100M price reflects how urgently large software vendors want proven agentic AI talent applied to unglamorous but highly profitable legacy infrastructure.

The technology is agentic, not just chatbot-style: Geniez's AI agents run directly on mainframes, observing live systems, diagnosing incidents and executing operational workflows through natural language, which is a step beyond simple code assistants or documentation search.

The founders have done this before: Peleg and Shprung previously founded Model9, a mainframe data management company acquired by BMC in 2023. That track record likely shortened Rocket's due diligence and raised the deal's valuation.

Skills shortage is the real driver: Rocket frames the acquisition around the retiring mainframe workforce, aiming to turn institutional knowledge into automation so fewer specialists are needed for mission-critical operations.

Rocket EVA is the landing spot: Geniez's team and tech will feed Rocket EVA, Rocket's agentic AI platform for core systems, extending AI into production mainframe workloads with governance and control.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this deal signals that agentic AI's fastest path to revenue may be unglamorous legacy infrastructure, not consumer apps. Investors are rewarding small, domain-expert teams that can automate high-stakes enterprise workflows. For developers, it highlights demand for skills at the intersection of AI agents, systems programming and mainframe operations; pure prompt-engineering roles may matter less than understanding z/OS, security and governance. For regular users, the impact is indirect but real: banks, insurers and airlines could see faster incident resolution, fewer outages and slower cost growth as AI assists the shrinking pool of mainframe experts. It also reinforces a consolidation trend where large enterprise software vendors buy small AI teams rather than build from scratch.
report.tools: To follow this space, watch Rocket EVA, Rocket Software's agentic AI platform for core systems. Open-source options include Zowe, the Open Mainframe Project's framework for modern mainframe interfaces and APIs; Ansible collections for z/OS automation; and IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z for COBOL-to-Java translation. For building agents, LangChain, LlamaIndex and CrewAI are common starting points. BMC AMI Cloud (formerly Model9) is also worth tracking given the founders' history.
